Olkusz New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Olkusz, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Olkusz dates to the early 14th century, with two Jewish-inhabited houses recorded before 1317; population reached 2,703 (40.6%) by 1921, mostly murdered at Auschwitz-Birkenau during WWII. This newer cemetery, probably established no earlier than the mid-19th century, remained in use into the 1940s - Róża Lender, who died in 1947, was among its last burials. Postwar destruction accelerated in 1946; the Olkusz Jewish Committee flagged the urgent need to repair the broken fence, and the City Council installed a makeshift barbed-wire replacement in 1948. Ownership transferred to the State Treasury under abandoned-property law; 2010 restoration cleaned the site, re-erected some matzevot, and rebuilt the fence. Just 22 people remained registered with Olkusz's Jewish Committee by June 1946, gradually leaving in subsequent years.
